title: Hoggenoch
summary: Hoggenoch is a correction, not a traditional Indigenous placename. The form was applied to Little Hog Neck near Sag Harbor and came from a mistaken spelling of Hog Neck in the 1686 Dongan Patent for Southampton.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Hoggenoch - Manhansett Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The 1665 deed for Hoggenoch (North Haven) reveals that while the Shelter Island Indians confirmed the transfer of the land, they explicitly retained their permanent rights to hunt, fish, and fowl. This legal stipulation demonstrates how Native peoples actively used early colonial agreements to protect their traditional subsistence practices and ensure ongoing access to their ancestral territories.
history_content: Hoggenoch belongs to the history of colonial record keeping and copying errors, not to a secure Indigenous placename tradition. The correction matters because a mistaken spelling of Hog Neck should not be repeated as Native language.
translation_content:
No Indigenous translation is supported for Hoggenoch. Hoggenoch or Hoggenock is treated as a corrupted form of the English place-name Hog Neck, also associated with Little Hog Neck near Sag Harbor.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names also express tangibly the human activity of investing the landscape with meaning and memory.”

— Marie Tehan, Victorian Geographic Place Names Bill statement, quoted in Ben Wilkie, ‘Rights, Reconciliation, and the Restoration of Djabwurrung and Jardwadjali Names to Grampians–Gariwerd’ (1998), Victorian Historical Journal 89(1), page 129
land_loss_content: Correcting Hoggenoch prevents a colonial copying error from being mistaken for an Indigenous placename. The correction keeps attention on the actual Hog Neck history while avoiding a false language claim.
whereintheworld_content: The map shape is broad because the exact location is uncertain. The source places the pseudo-name at Little Hog Neck near Sag Harbor, but the exact relationship between this mapped area, Hog Neck, and Little Hog Neck remains uncertain.
